subject: Nimbus POC: integration plan & success criteria

Subject: Nimbus POC: integration plan & success criteria

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed plan for the 4-week POC/trial so we can get your engineers ramped and the evaluation moving:

POC objective
- Validate Redwood-powered summarization + EHR enrichment in the Nimbus clinical triage flow, with latency <= 500ms median and accuracy aligned to your sample set.

Success criteria (what Nimbus will use to accept the POC)
1) Functional: End-to-end flow that consumes a patient note, calls Redwood for structured summary + candidate ICD tags, and returns results to the triage UI.
2) Quality: >= 85% agreement with Nimbus clinical labels on the provided evaluation set (50 sample notes).
3) Performance: median inference latency <= 500ms for 90% of requests at 1 RPS, and no more than 2% error rate during a 1-hour soak.
4) Security/compliance: Data is encrypted in transit, keys are customer-managed in Private deployments if requested, and audit logs are available for sampling.

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): Access + baseline run — exchange API keys, share sample notes, and confirm success criteria.
- Week 1: Integration + smoke tests — Redwood SDK integration, simple end-to-end test harness, basic quality checks.
- Week 2: Load testing + quality tuning — run 1 RPS soak, collect latency/accuracy metrics, adjust tokenization/prompt templates.
- Week 3: Final evaluation & wrap — produce evaluation report, demo, and next-steps discussion.

Ownership (who does what)
- Nimbus: provide sample notes, EHR connector details, and a technical contact for engineering syncs (Sara / Tom).
- Redwood: integration guide, SDK samples, an internal SE (Dylan) for engineering support, and monitoring/runbook for the trial.

Technical integration plan (high level)
- SDK: We recommend using our Java SDK for a quick integration (attached sample).
- API routes: /v1/generate for structured outputs; /v1/stream for low-latency streaming responses when you need partial summaries.
- Streaming: supports SSE/chunked streaming for progressive UI updates.
- Tool calling: we support structured tool calls (JSON) so the model can call your internal EHR lookup service (e.g., tool: ehr_lookup({patient_id})) and receive structured results.

Attachments included: integration-checklist.pdf and redwood-java-sdk-sample.zip (SDK + quickstart).

Next steps
1) Please confirm acceptance of the success criteria above or call out any changes by EOD Mon.
2) Sara — can you share the list of sample notes and the technical contact for the EHR connector?
3) If that looks good, I’ll schedule a 60-min engineering kickoff (we propose Tue 12/08 at 10am PT).

Thanks — looking forward to moving fast.

Best,

Ben — thanks for the clear plan. A few implementation notes for Sara and the Nimbus engineers to expedite the Week 1 integration:

High-level steps
1) Install SDK: we provide Java/Node/Python samples in the attached zip. Minimal code to create a client:

// Java sample (excerpt)
RedwoodClient client = RedwoodClient.builder()
  .apiKey(System.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
  .region("us-west-2")
  .build();

2) Endpoints to hit
- POST /v1/generate — request body: {"model":"redwood-2.1","input":"...","response_schema":"jsonSchema"} — returns structured summary + tags.
- POST /v1/stream — open an SSE stream for progressive tokens. Use for UI loading states.
- POST /v1/tool-call — used when the model asks to run an external function (we'll show examples).

3) Streaming details
- We support chunked streaming over HTTP and SSE. For the triage UI, open /v1/stream and consume partial summaries, then finalize when the stream closes. Latency is dominated by model decode; typical per-token overhead is small.

4) Tool calling pattern
- Provide the EHR lookup as an authenticated internal HTTP service. When the model returns a tool call, the SDK emits a structured JSON: {"tool":"ehr_lookup","args":{"patient_id":"..."}}. Your service should return structured JSON that we forward into the model context.

5) Authentication & keys
- For the POC we’ll issue an API key scoped to the trial. If you require KMS/HSM or Private deployment (customer-managed keys), we can scope next steps with our Solutions Architect.

Attachments: redwood-java-sdk-sample.zip (contains quickstart & examples), integration-checklist.pdf.

If useful, I can carve out a 90-min engineering office hours slot on Tue 12/08 for hands-on pairing to get the SDK running.

- Data residency: For the POC we can use the Redwood hosted API, but please confirm that logs are not persisted beyond the trial or that we can redact PHI. Also, can you confirm region: us (us-west)?
- Streaming reliability: We rely on progressive updates in the UI. Can you share any guidance on retry logic for SSE drops (e.g., resume token support)?
- Procurement: procurement@nimbushealth.com — we will loop them in for the standard NDA/PO.

I’ve attached our Nimbus_Security_Questionnaire.pdf with a few baseline items — would you have someone on the security team review?

On implementation: Dylan — the tool-calling approach looks promising for our ehr_lookup. Our backend team will implement an authenticated endpoint to accept the SDK's tool call requests.

Sara — perfect, thanks for the fast turnaround and for sending the questionnaire. Quick answers and final confirmations: 

- Region & logs: We will run the trial against our us-west region. For the POC we can enable request-level redaction of PHI on ingestion and set a 30-day auto-delete for logs; I’ve asked our security lead to review the attached questionnaire.

- SSE retry/resume: We support resume tokens for streaming sessions; if a connection drops you can re-open /v1/stream with a resume_token param. Dylan will include a short snippet in the office hours pairing.

- Engineering sync: Tue 12/08 at 11:00 AM PT — I’ll send a calendar invite.
